info.name: Zimal Store — Seller Onboarding (Phase 9: Retention & Renaming)
info.description:
Phase 9 manual test — the last two gaps in the Seller domain.

BEFORE YOU START
1) php artisan migrate
2) keep `php artisan queue:work` running
3) an APPROVED, ACTIVE store owned by {{seller_email}}
4) an admin {{admin_email}} who does NOT own it (C12)
5) run 1a first — it saves {{store_id}} and {{current_name}}

WHAT IS HERE
Folder 1-3  renaming a live store (14b). C6 locked store_name at
            approval, which was right — the admin verified it — but
            'forever' was wrong. Businesses rebrand.
Folder 4    KYC retention (14a). Almost no endpoints: it is a nightly
            command. The folder description is the real test plan.

THE ONE THING WORTH WATCHING: folder 3. Uniqueness is checked when the
name is REQUESTED and again inside the approval transaction, because
another store can take that name while the request sits in the queue.
Checking only once is the classic race that ends with two stores sharing
a name and a UNIQUE index blowing up in an admin's face.

variable.description: Optional — a manager of the same store (Phase 7), for E1.
A renewal you purged by hand — see folder 4.

item.name: 1a. My store now — saves store_id and current_name

request.description: Note data.store_name. Everything below compares against it.

Owner only (P9-5): a manager runs the shop, but its NAME is the
business's identity.

C45 — watch the response: data.store_name is STILL the old name, and
data.pending_name.requested is the new one. A request is not a rename;
nothing customer-facing moves until an admin approves.

The name on the verified DOCUMENTS never changes — only the storefront
name customers see.

item.name: 1c. Asking again while one is pending -> 409

request.description: One request at a time. Withdraw it first to ask for something else.

No notification and no audit entry for a withdrawal: nothing ever
changed that anyone else saw (C45).
Re-ask so the admin folder has something to review.

Oldest request first — the same fairness rule as the renewal queue.

Note this ordering is exclusive with the normal newest-first browse
list. Chaining both quietly produced a list sorted twice (C47).

Runs the uniqueness check AGAIN, inside the transaction on a locked row
(C44). See folder 3 for why that is not paranoia.

item.name: 2c. The seller sees the new name

request.description: store_name is the new one and pending_name is gone.

item.name: 2d. Reject path — ask again, then refuse it

request.description: Run this, then 2e.
A refusal the seller cannot act on is useless to them.
The store keeps the name it already had; the reason is emailed.

item.name: 3. C44 — the race the second check exists for
item.description:
HOW TO REPRODUCE, in order:

1) As the seller, ask for a name — say 'Rival Name' (request 3a).
2) While it sits in the queue, give that EXACT name to a DIFFERENT
   store. Easiest in the DB:
     UPDATE seller_profiles SET store_name = 'Rival Name' WHERE id = <other id>;
3) Run 3b. The approval is refused with 422.

WHY IT MATTERS: store_name carries a UNIQUE index. If approval trusted
the check made at request time, this would reach the database and throw
a raw integrity-constraint error in the admin's face — and with two
admins clicking at once, could put two stores on the same name.

After 3b the request is still PENDING and nothing was renamed, so the
seller can withdraw it and pick another name.

item.name: 3a. Ask for a name someone is about to take

request.description: Then do step 2 above before running 3b.
Refused at the second check, not at the database.

item.name: 3c. The request survived, nothing was renamed

request.description: pending_name is still there; store_name is untouched.

item.name: 4. KYC retention (14a)
item.description:
This is a nightly command, not an API. Almost nothing here is clickable —
the test plan is this description.

WHY IT EXISTS: we collected CNIC scans and bank statements and never
deleted any of them. A seller rejected five times left five copies of
their identity document on disk forever.

WHY IT WAS ONLY POSSIBLE NOW: deleting needs a clock, and a clock needs
a moment when the relationship ENDS. Store closure (Phase 8b) created
that moment. A quiet seller is still a seller (C41) — inactivity is
never the trigger.

THE RULE IS: DELETE THE FILE, KEEP THE ROW (P9-2). Every row still says
a document existed, who reviewed it and when, plus file_purged_at.
Deleting rows would destroy the KYC history we must be able to show.

TWO CLOCKS
  superseded_retention_days (90)  a rejected renewal, or an approved one
                                  a newer approved one replaced. Proves
                                  nothing current.
  kyc_retention_days (1825)       everything belonging to a store that
                                  CLOSED longer ago than this.
Both are config: SELLER_SUPERSEDED_RETENTION_DAYS and
SELLER_KYC_RETENTION_DAYS.

*** 1825 days (5 years) is the common AML/KYC figure. It has NOT been
checked against Pakistani law, and nobody here is a lawyer. Confirm it
before launch — changing it is one .env value, which is why it is
config and not a literal. ***

TO TEST BY HAND
  1) note a renewal's id and file_path, and confirm the file exists under
     storage/app/private/seller-renewals/
  2) age it past the window:
       UPDATE seller_document_renewals
          SET status='rejected', updated_at = DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 100 DAY)
        WHERE id = <id>;
  3) php artisan seller:purge-expired-kyc-documents
  4) the file is gone from disk, the ROW is still there, and
     file_purged_at is set
  5) run it again — nothing changes. It is idempotent on purpose (C43):
     file first, stamp second, so a crash in between leaves the next run
     something it can finish rather than an orphaned file nothing points
     at.

WHAT MUST NEVER BE PURGED
  - a SUSPENDED store's documents, whatever the dates (C42). Suspension
    usually means an investigation is open; destroying evidence then is
    the worst possible timing.
  - the newest approved renewal of each type — that is current evidence.
  - an active store's onboarding documents, however old.

item.name: 4a. Downloading a purged document -> 404 with a clear reason

request.description:
Set {{renewal_id}} to a renewal you purged in step 3 above.

The message says the file was deleted under the retention policy and
the record of it is kept — not a vague 'not found', which would look
like a bug.

item.name: 4b. Closed stores can be filtered for

request.description:
C46 — this list used to validate `in:active,suspended`, typed out by
hand. 'closed' was added to the enum in Phase 8b and the list did not
follow, so closed stores were silently unfilterable. It now derives
from the enum.

This is also how you find the stores whose retention clock is running.

Set the body to a name you know is taken. Checked against BOTH

a frozen application row carrying the name it was approved under, and
that row keeps its claim on it.
